file_id: Sri. B.Devender, vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2025

sentences.text: Sri. B.Devender, vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2025

The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Writ Petition No.22619 of 2025
Order:

Aggrieved by the inaction of respondent No.3 on the petitioner's representation dated 24.03.2025 requesting to allot alternate land in Muduchintalpally Mandal of Keesara Revenue Division of Medchal- Malkajgiri District.

A consequential prayer is sought to direct respondent No.3 to take action on the said representation and also on the letter addressed by respondent No.2 (CCLA)
directing to examine on the petitioner's representation for allotment / assignment of alternate land for Ac.10-00 guntas in Muduchintalpally Mandal of Keesara Revenue Division of Medchal-Malkajgiri District.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. L.Ravinder, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue and learned counsel representing the learned Standing Counsel for TGIIC appearing for respondent No.7.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner's father was allotted an agricultural land to an extent of Ac.10-00 guntas in Survey No.542 of Muduchintalpally Mandal.
The then revenue authorities issued proceedings in File No.B/692/1992, dated 18.11.1992 in favor of petitioner's father.
Since then, the petitioner's father was in peaceful possession of the allotted land and was doing cultivation till 2003.

Subsequently, the then authorities had forcibly taken the said possession and initiated land acquisition proceedings for setting up industrial park in Survey No.542 in the Muduchintalpally Mandal, without issuing any notice to the petitioner's father, who was allotted the said land.
He further submitted that petitioner's father expired on 06.11.2005.

Subsequent to which the petitioner made a representation on 24.03.2025 for allotment of alternate land or to pay compensation to the petitioner under the provision of Land Acquisition Act, 2013 through respondent No.3, being one of the legal heirs of his father.
Aggrieved by the inaction of revenue authorities, the petitioner is constrained to file this writ petition seeking appropriate directions.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submitted that the alleged allotment was made in the year 1992 and it is stated that the same was taken over by the revenue authorities in the year 2003 and the present writ petition has been filed after an inordinate delay of more than two decades, without any explanation for such delay.
Hence, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches.
It is further submitted that the petitioner's father or his legal heirs did not raise any objection at the relevant stage, the claim for compensation or alternate land cannot be entertained.

The representation dated 24.03.2025 made by the petitioner cannot revive a stale and time-barred claim and mere submission of representation after several years does not give rise to a fresh cause of action.
Except the alleged proceedings dated 18.11.1992, no relevant record has been produced to establish that the petitioner's father was in actual possession of the said land.

It is Sri. B.Devender, vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35697427/
1 further submitted that if the petitioner claims compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013,
he must approach the competent authority under the said Act and establish his entitlement in accordance with law.

sentences.text: The prayer seeking allotment of alternate land or compensation is wholly misconceived in the absence of any subsisting right or enforceable claim.
Hence, the writ petition is devoid of merit and liable to be dismissed.

5. This Court, having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, does not see any merits in the contentions of the petitioner's counsel and the submissions made in his affidavit in the writ petition are devoid of merits and the same is liable to be dismissed.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications if any pending, in this petition, shall stand closed.

____________________ E.V.VENUGOPAL, J Date: 06.11.2025 Nsk Sri. B.Devender, vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35697427/
